A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural-operator stress-testing study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the consolidated numerical summaries.

before.justification: v4 reports original evaluations of 750 trained models across three architectures and five PDE families, with empirical figures and degradation statistics in Appendix A.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical evaluations in its results figures and Appendix B, alongside newly added theoretical material.

M1.justification: The stress-testing framework, FNO, DeepONet-style and CNO models, architecture configurations, training approach and evaluation without fine-tuning are retained. Added explanations and theoretical propositions do not introduce an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate nonlinear Schrödinger, Poisson, Navier–Stokes, Black–Scholes and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky under the same applicable stress-test categories. The resolution-direction wording changes within an existing test; newly discussed benchmarks and architecture families are not evaluated.

E2.justification: FNO, DeepONet and CNO remain the evaluated comparator set in every corresponding PDE comparison. The expanded related-work citations introduce no additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes resolution evaluation from finer resolutions in v4 to finer or coarser resolutions in v7. This is a limited reported protocol expansion, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Training budgets, model sizes, sample counts, baseline rollout length and degradation metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing stress-test analyses and plotted comparisons are retained. The new mechanism explanations and proofs add no empirical ablation, robustness experiment or diagnostic result; merging the existing plots changes their presentation.

E5.justification: v4 Appendix A explicitly states that initialization and randomly generated training and evaluation data vary across runs; v7 omits this account of variability. Both retain 50 runs per architecture–PDE pair and report means, standard deviations and 95% confidence intervals.

E6.justification: All 54 degradation rows, including their means, standard deviations and confidence bounds, match between v4 Tables 1–5 and v7 Appendix B Table 1. However, v7 Section 5 adds an overbroad statement that all three models degrade in the discussed Navier–Stokes and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky rollout settings, despite the retained DeepONet Kuramoto–Sivashinsky factor of 0.886, with CI [0.847, 0.924].

T1.justification: v7 adds Section 5.1 and Appendix A: a rollout composition bound under uniform approximation and Lipschitz assumptions, and a resolution-risk decomposition using a Fourier spectral-tail bound and an approximate empirical-risk-minimization argument. Both propositions receive proofs, including an auxiliary Sobolev spectral-tail lemma. These formal results are absent from v4.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a reusable stress-testing framework and evidence that baseline accuracy does not reliably predict robustness across architectures, PDEs and shifts. v7 foregrounds these findings in the abstract and introduction, but they were already stated in v4's results and conclusion.

C2.justification: v7 Sections 4–5 add substantial explanations linking spectral mixing, local multiscale response, branch–trunk conditioning and repeated composition to individual PDE outcomes, while qualifying these as interpretations rather than causal proofs. It also removes v4's explicit warnings about limited PDE coverage and the need for architecture-specific tuning and matched budgets before superiority claims.

D1.justification: v7 specifies perturbations to state channels, describes spectral summaries as frequency-binned, and mentions aggregation of raw seed outputs into summaries and figures. These refine documentation of existing procedures. Hyperparameters, hardware and the stated code-access location remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially, covering operator-learning theory, additional architecture families, domain generalization and adaptation, discontinuities, boundary conditioning, and benchmarks such as PDEBench, APEBench, The Well and SIMSHIFT. v7 explicitly positions the framework relative to these efforts and the scientific foundation-model agenda, beyond v4's narrower overview.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology and discussion undergo extensive rewriting. The introductory PDE list becomes compact prose, the discussion is reorganized around mechanisms, and acknowledgements, references and appendices are restructured. Author and publication-header information also changes.

P2.justification: v7 merges v4 Figures 2–3 into a four-panel Figure 2, restructures Figure 1 with subcaptions, and relocates the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky plot. Five separate six-column appendix tables become one consolidated four-column table using mean±standard-deviation and interval columns. These substantially reorganize existing displays without adding numerical results.

improvement.justification: The explicit assumptions and proofs in Section 5.1 and Appendix A, together with stronger comparisons to relevant prior work, provide a limited overall gain in explanatory grounding. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. Removed fairness and variability disclosures, and the overbroad rollout statement despite DeepONet's Kuramoto–Sivashinsky factor below one, temper that gain.
